title: Mind × Ecosystems
content_html:
Mind × Ecosystems

  • Mind as an Ecosystem — The mind is like a forest: structure + dynamic interactions = emergent properties.
  • Ecosystem Memory — Ecosystems “remember” via legacies (seed banks, soils, networks) shaping recovery.
  • Wetlands Workflow — Capture/compose photography guided by ecological memory (seed banks ↔ image layering).
  • Panarchy — Adaptive cycles (growth → conservation → release → reorganization) nested across scales.
  • Embedded Memory × Evolutionary Psych — Plant legacies + animal memory systems co‑produce resilience.
  • Working Together — Conscious (animals) and non‑conscious (plants, microbes) cooperation creates emergent harmony.
  • Beyond Plants/Animals — Ecosystems = plants + animals + humans + microbes + fungi + soils + climate + energy.
Essay Core Idea Application
Mind as an Ecosystem Mind mirrors ecosystems: embedded memory + feedback = emergence. Philosophical parallel for memory/consciousness art.
Ecosystem Memory Ecosystems store history in physical/biological legacies. Framework for resilience + wetlands art metaphor.
Wetlands Workflow Translate ecological memory into capture + compositing plan. Photo/video layering, SJT sequencing, QA checklist.
Panarchy — Theory Nested adaptive cycles (r, K, Ω, α) govern transformation. Bridge to memory’s select–change–reconstruct cycle.
Panarchy Helper Processing schema (CSV fields, SJT presets, blend modes). Turn theory into generative art/FFmpeg pipeline.
Embedded Memory × Evolutionary Psych Animals recall; plants embed; together they stabilise ecosystems. Table of plants vs. animals, cross‑scale memory alignment.
Working Together Cooperation emerges across conscious/non‑conscious spectrum. Examples: pollination, seed caching, mycorrhizae.
Beyond Plants/Animals Abiotic + microbial + fungal forces are equally central. Diagram and citations expanding system boundaries.

Glossary

  • Ecological memory — The way past states/events persist in ecosystems (seed banks, soil, structures).
  • Panarchy — A model of nested adaptive cycles (growth, conservation, release, reorganization) across scales.
  • Adaptive memory — Evolutionary psychology idea: memory is biased toward survival/reproductive relevance.
  • Mutualism — Interaction where both partners benefit (pollination, mycorrhizae).
  • Trophic cascade — Top‑down effects of predators that indirectly shape plants and ecosystems.
  • Abiotic — Non‑living ecosystem components: soil, water, air, climate, nutrients, energy.
  • SJT permutations — Steinhaus–Johnson–Trotter algorithm: minimal‑change ordering of permutations for smooth frame sequences.
